claims.hypothesis: Radio jets in z>5 radio-loud quasars disturb host morphology/kinematics (e.g. mergers)
claims.experiment: Band 7 [CII] and continuum imaging of five RL quasars at ~1.0-1.4'' resolution with Gaussian line fits and moment maps
claims.result: Sizes consistent with beam sizes; single-Gaussian spectra; no extended or perturbed structure
claims.finding: No strong evidence for mergers in the newly observed RL quasar hosts, though resolution and SNR are limited

evidence.quote: we do not recover perturbed/extended morphologies or kinematics, signatures of potential mergers

claims.hypothesis: Radio jets suppress or alter [CII] emission in RL quasar hosts relative to RQ hosts
claims.experiment: Compared [CII] luminosity, SFR, EW, FWHM of RL (this work + literature) vs 76 RQ quasars with KS tests
claims.result: L_CII and SFR_[CII] slightly lower for RL (p=0.04); EW and FWHM consistent (p=0.24, 0.14)

claims.hypothesis: The ~1 mm continuum of high-z RL quasars includes non-thermal synchrotron emission
claims.experiment: Built radio-to-sub-mm SEDs from literature radio, RACS/FLASH and new ALMA fluxes and extrapolated radio power laws to ~300 GHz
claims.result: Estimated synchrotron fractions ~2% to ~100% (>9% in at least four sources)
claims.finding: Continuum arises from a mix of synchrotron and dust in at least four cases; dust-derived quantities should be treated with caution

Hence, extreme caution should be taken when deriving dust properties (luminosities, masses, SFR) for these objects.

referee_caveats_inferred: Internal inconsistencies: PSO135+16 redshift is 5.63 in the sample table but 5.68 in the text; 1D-fit table gives F_cont 0.064+/-0.10 mJy and PSO352-15 F_line 1.20+/-0.040 Jy km/s, which differ from the 2D-fit table values
M_dust for PSO055-00 with synchrotron subtracted (3.8e7) exceeds the total-continuum value (2.8e7), which should not happen
Synchrotron fractions rely on non-simultaneous radio data and extrapolated power laws without a full SED fit
Fixed T_dust=47 K and beta=1.6 and a single alpha_CII conversion carry large systematic uncertainty for AGN hosts
The L_CII difference rests on p=0.04 with only five new RL sources plus a handful from the literature and a heterogeneous RQ comparison sample; multiple KS tests are not corrected
M_dyn assumes a single median inclination of 46 deg for unresolved sources and a dispersion-dominated geometry
Companion non-detection is weakly informative because the data are shallow

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Seven short Cycle 7 compact-array executions (on-source 726-3810 s each); likely ~10-30 GB raw in total, a few GB of calibrated MS.
reproducibility.score_reason: Project code and key choices (robust=2, uvcontsub, apertures, T_dust, beta, equations, final tables) are given, but imaging parameters, line-free channels and radio-SED inputs are missing, and comparison sample values come from many external papers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: A single named Cycle 7 project, pipeline products, standard Gaussian fits and closed-form equations, with numeric tables for [CII] fluxes, continuum and derived L_CII/SFR/M_dyn; the SED synchrotron part is harder.
